schema.note: An episode is an ordered list of beats. Beats block: each one finishes before the next starts, because a scripted scene whose steps overlap is a race, not a scene. This file is shaped for UnityEngine.JsonUtility, which is why 'Kind' is an integer and not a string -- JsonUtility deserialises enums from numbers only. 'KindName' and 'Note' sit beside them for humans and are ignored by the parser. Do not delete the integers.

beatKinds.1: FadeOut   -- cover the screen. Seconds is the fade length.
beatKinds.2: FadeIn    -- reveal. Seconds is the fade length.
beatKinds.4: Dialogue  -- play the sequence named by Id from dialogue.json, block until it ends. Target='starter' means: suffix Id with '_' + the chosen starter's game species id, so one beat can resolve to one of three authored sequences.
beatKinds.5: TakeControl -- freeze the player, flow to Cutscene.
beatKinds.7: MoveActor -- walk the actor named by Id to the marker named by Target, block until it arrives. The actor faces the player on arrival. Seconds is a timeout, not a duration: if the walk has not finished by then, snap and continue, so blocked geometry can never strand the scene.
beatKinds.8: CameraTo  -- swing the camera's YAW toward the object named by Id (OverworldCameraRig.LookToward). Kept working for backwards compatibility, but know what it is: it only sets the orbital rig's yaw from the player's position -- pitch stays 8 deg, the boom stays 8.5 m -- so it can point at something and it cannot COMPOSE anything. The act's authored framings now use CameraShot (19) / PlayTimeline (20); reach for CameraTo only when 'roughly toward that thing from wherever the player stands' is genuinely the shot.
beatKinds.9: ChooseStarter -- open the starter choice, block until the player commits. StarterSelection.Commit runs InitialiseNewGame, so this beat is the point of no return.
beatKinds.10: GiveItem -- Id is a FieldItems id, Amount is the count.
beatKinds.11: SetFlag  -- Id is the flag, Value is on/off. Flags gate episodes, NPC dialogue variants and the gate ramp.
beatKinds.12: Battle   -- Target='starter_counter' fights the trainer named by Id with a party built from StarterOption.RivalCounterSpeciesId. Target='staged' fights the creature a StageCreature beat put on the ground -- a wild battle, at that creature's own species and level, routed through EncounterDirector so the creature is removed from the world afterwards. Id is ignored in the staged case.
beatKinds.13: AskName  -- opens name entry, blocks, writes PlayerProfile.SetTrainerName. Id is the default used if the player confirms an empty field or the UI does not exist yet. Target names the profile field.
beatKinds.14: StageCreature -- NEW. Stand a wild creature on the marker named by Id. Target is its GAME species id as a string (SliceRoster, not national dex -- game 25 is Rattata), Amount is its level. It is placed visible, facing the player, and held still: it does not wander, does not react and cannot start a battle on its own. At most one at a time. Destroyed when the act ends, on every path -- but handed across a NextEpisodeId chain rather than destroyed between links, because field_bag_left stages the ambusher precisely so field_ambush can fight it; the last episode of the chain is the one whose end clears it.
beatKinds.15: CreatureApproach -- NEW. Walk the staged creature up to the player and block until it is 1.6 m away. Seconds is a timeout, as with MoveActor: an approach that does not land is snapped, because the beat after it is a battle that needs the creature on screen.
beatKinds.16: MoveActorToPlayer -- NEW. Walk the actor named by Id to the player's shoulder and block until they are there. Seconds is a timeout, as with MoveActor; Value false means do not turn to face the player on arrival. Exists because the marks live in cast.json and the player does not: the friend who has to be standing beside them when the grass moves has no mark to walk to, and authoring one would pin the shot to a spot the player may not be standing on.
beatKinds.17: StageRing -- NEW. Ring the player, and the actor named by Id when there is one, with wild creatures; Value false takes the ring away again with a scatter rather than a blink. Target is the game species id and defaults to the staged creature's own, so the ring is that creature's flock. Amount is how many, clamped 3-12. SECONDS IS THE RADIUS IN METRES on this beat and not a wait -- it does not wait for anything. Placed on the navmesh, deterministically from the beat, facing inward, and held still: they cannot wander and cannot start a battle by touching anybody. Removed when the episode ends on every path.
beatKinds.18: ExitActor -- NEW. Send the actor named by Id away toward the marker named by Target and stop drawing them the moment the camera can no longer see them. The marker is the DIRECTION they left in, not the end of the journey: past it they keep walking the same bearing until they are out of shot. Seconds is a ceiling, and overrunning it is an error rather than a warning, because it means somebody was removed in full view. Value true takes them off the screen; Value false leaves them drawn and standing on the mark, which is how a walk the navmesh cannot carry -- the town/field seam -- gets finished off camera instead of stalling in frame.
beatKinds.19: CameraShot -- NEW. Frame a genuinely COMPOSED shot: Id names a shot in shots.json, and the cinematics layer places an aimed, deoccluded CinemachineCamera from that authored composition (fixed position + look-at, or an orbit around a runtime-resolved object -- Actor_StagedCreature, Prop_ProfessorBag, the player) on the episode-shot priority rung. The shot is HELD until the next CameraShot/PlayTimeline replaces it, a GiveControl beat runs, or the episode ends -- the runner's finally releases it on every path, and a NextEpisodeId chain hands the held shot across the seam the way it hands the staged creature. Target is the marker the beat degrades to (a plain CameraTo yaw swing) when the cinematics layer or shots.json is missing, so the scene still points somewhere. The dialogue conversation camera outbids this rung for the length of a line and drops back; the shot keeps its state while outbid.
beatKinds.20: PlayTimeline -- NEW. Play the generated TimelineAsset named by Id (Resources/Timelines, built by Tools/Poké Lab/Rebuild/Sequencing Timelines from shots.json) through the cinematics layer's director, blocking. Seconds is a CEILING, not a duration -- it defaults to the asset's own length plus two seconds, and on overrun the choreography is jumped to its final frame rather than abandoned mid-move. The final frame is then held exactly like a CameraShot. Target is the CameraTo fallback marker, as with 19. Asset missing: log, degrade to the yaw swing, spend no time.

episodeFields.CompletionFlag: set when the episode's beats genuinely run to the end -- and ONLY then. It used to be set in the runner's finally unconditionally, failure included, which guaranteed flags like story.pokedex at the cost of the opposite failure: an episode interrupted halfway (exception in a beat, coroutine stopped) was stamped as seen, could never be offered again, and the save was permanently short one scene with nothing on screen to say so. Now an interrupted episode leaves its flag unset, its StoryEncounter re-offers it (StoryEncounter checks this flag after the runner returns), and a chain link that died between sessions is resumed by the runner at startup. An episode with its flag set never replays, as before.
episodeFields.NextEpisodeId: Played immediately when this one finishes, in the same frame the previous one releases. Used only where two scenes are really one scene split for authoring. Read by Episode.NextEpisodeId in EpisodeRunner.cs -- the field was absent for a while, and JsonUtility drops what it has no field for without a word, so the chain authored here was silently discarded. Two runner rules keep a chain honest: an interrupted episode does not chain (its successor stays owed to the save rather than playing over a scene that never happened), and at startup the runner scans for any link whose predecessor's CompletionFlag is set while its own is not -- the save-quit hole, where a session ends between links and no StoryTrigger points at the successor -- and resumes the earliest such link.
episodeFields.Trigger: Advisory, and still not read by the runner. The live wiring is LevelLayoutBuilder.StoryTriggers, which hangs a StoryEncounter on the named actor at build time; this stays as the authored intent so the two can be compared. Keep them in step by hand -- nothing checks. NOTE: one StoryEncounter per actor. BuildStoryTriggers reuses the component it finds, so two triggers naming the same actor is not two beats, it is the second overwriting the first. Bram and Kes are each wanted twice, so each spends its one slot on the beat that has to be on the character -- Bram's refusal, and Kes' battle -- and the other beat hangs off a marker object nearby ('Trigger_GateOpen', 'Trigger_Square').

schema.actNote: The opening act, restructured. The shape is now: the player tries to leave, is turned back and told to find Kes; Kes sets a forfeit and bolts; the gate opens; the player finds Linden muttering on the lake bank; he leaves his bag; a creature that is already standing in the grass walks up to them; they take a ball out of the bag under pressure and fight it; Linden comes back and gives them the dex. Everything that used to happen at the town gate -- the case on the ground, the flock, the choice, the rival battle -- has moved or gone. The single biggest change is that the first battle is against a creature the player watched approach, not a cut to a battle screen.
gaps: AskName (13) falls through to its Id ('Ren') when nothing presents it. NameEntryPresenter exists now, so this is only a fallback.
Dialogue text uses a {PLAYER} token; EpisodeRunner.Substitute replaces it.

'vfx.kes_runs' (kes_summons line 3) and 'vfx.professor_leaves' (field_professor_mutters line 4) have no listener. Both are the cue for the actor to move, and until something listens the MoveActor beat has to come after the whole dialogue -- so Kes walks away one line after the script has already said he is gone. When a listener exists, drive the run from the event and turn these MoveActor beats into snaps.

There is no authored line between the starter being taken and the battle starting. op_choice_result_* were Linden's read on the one you took plus Kes announcing the counter, and neither of them is on the bank. The choice is silent by design now rather than by omission -- see the ChooseStarter note -- but the beat after it could still use one, and it would have to be Kes'. StarterPresenter used to wait twenty seconds for op_choice_result before releasing its close-up, which timed out in full every time and held the shot over the top of the battle; it now holds for a fixed 1.6 s.

'story.case_open' is authored on op_professor_arrives, which nothing plays any more, so StarterPresenter's early-open path is dead and the case opens from the ChooseStarter beat instead. Harmless, and worth knowing before anyone goes looking for why the signal never fires.

Bram has no repeatable 'go and find Kes' line. gate_wait_for_kes is PlaysOnlyOnce, and dialogue.json's NpcBindings still default npc_gate_01 to gate_block_no_starter -- so a player who walks into the closed ramp a second time is told they have no Pokemon rather than that Kes is waiting.

RETIRED, and their dialogue with them: 'opening_departure' (op_rival_start, op_gate_block, op_flock, op_professor_arrives, op_choice_prompt, op_choice_result_1/_5/_10, op_handover) and 'leaving_town' (dex_handover, dex_close, and the two repels it granted). 'riv_after' went with the rival battle's Linden beats. None of that copy is reachable now.

Episodes.Note: Unchanged. Cold open: black screen, the professor's voice, the name, then the lab dome filling the top of the screen from the plaza spawn. Ends with control, and nothing to walk towards but the gate -- which is the point. The restructured act begins by letting the player try to leave and stopping them. Target length ~75s.

Beats.Note: Before anything. The player never has control during the prologue.

Guarantee black rather than trusting the boot state. 0.6s, not 0.0: when the boot cover is already up this fade is invisible either way, and when it is not -- a scene opened directly, a boot path that revealed early -- 0.0 was a hard cut to black on the first frame, which is the one thing the transition brief forbids. Sixty centiseconds is short enough not to delay the prologue and long enough to read as intent.

Framed behind the black, so the fade-in reveals the dome already composed -- and now it genuinely is: the old CameraTo could only yaw the exploration rig, which cut the dome off above the frame (verified in-editor). shot_lab_dome is a placed low-angle camera on the plaza, pitched 22 deg up at the dome, matching tl_opening_reveal's first key so the reveal and the push-in are one continuous frame. Target is the degraded path: no cinematics layer, and this is the old yaw swing again.
8 lines over black. Auto-advancing except the last two. ~32s.
2 lines. Uses {PLAYER}.
Slow. This is the shot the whole town was built around.

No text. Let the dome sit there -- then move. Replaces a bare 1.8 s Wait with the authored reveal: 1.2 s of hold and a 3.4 s push-in, scrubbable in the Timeline window. Ends held on the tighter frame, which the bulletin below plays under. Seconds 0 means the default ceiling, asset duration + 2 s.
The morning bulletin off the plaza research terminal. It names the mystery and points at the lake, which is where the act is going. 3 lines, ~11s.
Free on the plaza. Sela in the market row points at Kes if the player wanders; the gate is the other thing they can try, and trying it is now the next beat.

Episodes.Note: The first block, and it replaces the old 'you have no Pokemon' refusal outright. The difference matters: the old one was a rule, and a rule the player has not broken yet reads as the game distrusting them. This one is a message being passed on -- Bram is not stopping you, Kes is. Nothing is set here except that the refusal happened, and the ramp stays closed because StoryGate is still reading story.gate_open. Target length ~20s.

Beats.Note: 3 lines. Bram names the square, which is the only direction the player is given.

Episodes.Note:
The send-off. He walks over rather than speaking from his post, because being approached is the whole characterisation. He explains nothing, sets a forfeit and leaves -- and the forfeit is what carries the scene, because it is the only reason the player has to follow somebody who has not said where he is going. This is also where the ramp opens: the flag is set here, in the beat that earns it, rather than in a later scene that could be missed.

Triggered off a marker object in the square rather than off Kes himself, and the walk-over is a MoveActor beat instead of StoryEncounter's own approach. That looks like a downgrade and is not: NPC_Rival has exactly one StoryEncounter slot, and it is needed for the rival battle -- which is the one beat that has to sit on the same object as his TrainerController, or the sight cone and the story beat race each other for who gets to start the fight. See TrainerController.StandsDown. Target length ~40s. Kes leaves through the gate, not across it. He used to be sent straight from the square to his field post, and with the two bands baking separate navmeshes his agent simply headed for the straight line — out through the fence beside the ramp, in full view, which is the one shot this beat exists to sell. Mark_Rival_GateStand already stands at the head of the ramp, so the run is square -> gate -> field and only the last leg crosses the seam, off camera.

Beats.Note: He crosses the square and stops in front of the player, facing them -- MoveActor turns an actor to the player on arrival. This is the approach the trigger used to do for free. 3.97 m at NpcController's 1.4 m/s is 2.8 s of walking and the timeout was 4.0, which left nothing for the path being longer than the straight line or for the agent getting up to speed. Widened rather than moving the mark: the timeout is a last resort and should never be what ends a walk.

5 lines. Line 3 is the forfeit and carries EventId 'vfx.kes_runs'; line 4 is the player watching him go. Nothing listens for the event yet, which is why the walk below happens after the whole conversation instead of during it.

Read by StoryGate, which drops the wall across the ramp. Set here and not in 'gate_opens': that episode hangs off a trigger object at the ramp, and if the object is missing the player must still be able to leave.

BEFORE the walk-offs, not after. Holding the pad through twenty-four seconds of a boy walking away reads as a freeze -- the user called it one, twice. The player is free the moment the last line lands; Kes leaves under their feet, the way a friend actually leaves.

Waypoint. The navmesh's straight line from the square to the gate cuts behind the market row's houses -- with the walk now happening under the player's free camera, he was watched wading into the back-lot grass. This mark sits ON Path_TownMain; two street hops read as a boy using the road.

Square to the head of the ramp: 7.3 m in a straight line, more along the path, which is 5.2 s of walking at 1.4 m/s BEFORE the path is longer than the line -- against a timeout that was 5.0. So this beat ended in the snap every single time and said so: '[Episode] NPC_Rival did not reach Mark_Rival_GateStand within 5.0s and was snapped there.' Widened to 12 s rather than moving the mark closer, because the walk is the shot. Value false because he is leaving: MoveActor turns an actor to face the player on arrival, and a boy who has just shouted that he is counting must not stop at the gate and look back.

Down the ramp and gone. This was a MoveActor, and a MoveActor cannot make this journey: Town and Field bake their own navmeshes with nothing linking them, so his path stops dead at the seam at the bottom of the ramp -- and the old arrival test read the end of a truncated path as an arrival, so he 'arrived' there, silently, and stood at the bottom of the ramp for the rest of the act. That is the strange place he settled in. ExitActor walks him out of the Look_GateRamp shot and only then puts him on the field mark, so the part the navmesh cannot carry happens where nobody is looking. Value false: he stays drawn, because rival_first_battle waits for him at that mark.

Episodes.Note: Two lines at the top of the ramp on the way out. Deliberately load-bearing for nothing: the gate is already open by the time this plays, so a player who never triggers it loses a beat and not the act. It hangs off its own trigger object because Bram's one StoryEncounter slot is spent on gate_wait_for_kes -- see the Trigger note in the schema. Target length ~10s.

Beats.Note: 2 lines. The second is the only warning the player gets about the grass, and the thing in the grass is the next battle they fight.

Episodes.Note: The player's first sight of the professor is his back, mid-count. He does not stop being mid-thought because somebody arrived, and he does not explain the plot -- the whole scene is a man with forty-one records and a number that does not work. Approach is zero: he is seventy-one and standing still, and a professor who jogs at the player undoes the character. Target length ~45s.

Beats.Note: 5 lines. Line 4 carries EventId 'vfx.professor_leaves'. Nothing listens, so the walk is the beat below.
Before the walk-off, for the same reason as kes_summons: fourteen held seconds of an old man walking away reads as a freeze. The bag is on the bank either way; noticing it is the player's move.

He goes back to the town, and the mark is the direction rather than the destination. This was a MoveActor to the same mark and that is the whole of the fault: Mark_Prof_Offstage is 7.7 m away, so he walked seven metres, stopped, and -- because MoveActor turns an actor to face the player on arrival -- turned round and stood there looking at them for the rest of the scene, still in frame, with the walk cycle running because a parked agent's sprite was reading its speed off a smoothed position delta that never quite reached zero. ExitActor keeps him walking town-ward past the mark until the camera has lost him and then stops drawing him. He is put back on the mark as he goes, because that is verified ground with navmesh under it and 'field_professor_returns' brings him in from there.

Episodes.Note: One line, and then the creature is standing there. Split from 'field_ambush' rather than merged so the ambush can be judged -- and jumped to -- on its own, and chained so there is no frame between them in which the player could walk away. The creature is staged HERE, before the ambush's first line, because the scene is only worth anything if the thing was already in the grass: a creature that appears at the moment it is mentioned is a cut, and a cut is what this act exists to avoid. Target length ~15s.

Beats.Note: He comes over from his field post, 9 m away. Three of this scene's four lines are his and the one before it has Linden greeting '자네들' -- the script has had the two of them together in the field since it was written and the staging never brought him. So the bag was found, opened and exclaimed over by a boy who was standing on the shore trail the whole time.
1 line. An observation, not a decision -- the player is not offered the bag here, and the offer never comes; the ambush takes the decision away.

Rattata, level 4. GAME species id 25, from SliceRoster -- not the national dex number, which is the one mistake in this project that produces a plausible wrong creature rather than an error. It is in the route's own tall-grass table at levels 3-6, so this is a creature the grass could genuinely have produced, which is the whole reason it is a RoamingCreature and not a prop. Level 4 against a level 5 starter: winnable, and not a formality.

No text. The player looks at it before anything says it is there. Control is not handed back here: the episode chains straight into field_ambush, and the runner's finally is what guarantees control comes back if that chain ever fails.

Episodes.Note:
The moment the act is built to deliver, and the one rule it has is that nothing here is a cut. The creature was placed a beat ago and the player has already looked at it; now the rest of its flock walks out of the reeds and closes round the two of them, then it walks the distance itself on the same NavMesh everything else walks on, and only then does the battle open. The starter choice stays a menu and is deliberately not replaced by a 'take a ball' interaction -- see the note on the ChooseStarter beat.

RESTAGED. Everything the dialogue claimed was happening here used to be happening in the dialogue only: Kes was 9 m away on the shore trail while three of the lines were his, '우리 둘 다 둘러싸였어' was spoken to an empty bank, and -- because the episode that hands off to this one tore its own staging down a line before the hand-off -- there was not even the one creature in the grass. The beats now say what the lines say. Target length ~65s plus the battle.

Beats.Note: Defensive, and normally instant: 'field_bag_left' has already brought him over and a walk of nothing returns on the first frame. It is here because the schema's own note says this episode has to be judgeable -- and jumpable to -- on its own, and every line in it is written for two people standing together.

2 lines now, not 5 -- see the sequence's own note in dialogue.json. The grass moves and Kes yelps at the one creature that has been standing in it since the beat before. What used to be lines 2-4 has moved below, so that the encirclement can be staged in between.

THE ENCIRCLEMENT, and the reason this beat exists at all is that the line below it -- '야, 양쪽이야! 우리 둘 다 둘러싸였어!' -- has been in the script since the act was written and there has never been anything on screen to make it true. Seven of them at 4.5 m, centred on the midpoint of the player and Kes rather than on the player, so the friend is inside the circle with them and not watching from outside it. Expect fewer than seven to land: the bag is 2.41 m from the waterline and the navmesh excludes water, so the lake arc of the ring has nothing to stand on and is skipped with a note in the log. That is the right failure -- they came out of the grass, not out of the lake -- and it still closes the landward side, which is the side the player is facing. Target is empty, which means the staged creature's own species and level: these are its flock, and the one that walks out at the player in the next beat has to be one of the ones standing in the ring. They are held still -- they cannot wander and cannot open a battle by touching anybody, which matters because the player has no party yet.

1 line. Kes counts the ones that just walked out of the reeds. Played after the ring is up and before the ambusher closes, so the player reads it in that order: one of them, then all of them, then the one coming for you.
It closes the distance. 6s is a timeout and not a duration: an approach that snags on the reeds is snapped to 1.6 m rather than holding the player frozen watching it fail.

2 lines, the last of them Kes asking which one you are taking. This is the whole of the setup the choice gets, and the last voice heard before it -- the professor's prompt that used to sit in the box for the length of the choice is gone, because the player is taking a ball out of a stranger's bag with the owner over the hill.

Still the menu, and that is a decision rather than an omission. StarterSelection.Commit is InitialiseNewGame -- the party, the bag and the save all begin at this instant -- so replacing the choice with a GiveItem would leave the player holding a ball, with no party, in front of a battle they cannot fight. What changed is the fiction around it, and the fiction is carried by the line above and by what is standing round them: nobody is offering, the bag is not theirs, the creature is already there, and NOBODY IS SPEAKING. StarterPresenter puts one speaker-less line in the box for this beat and no name plate -- 몰래 고르는 것이라 -- see the class note there.
Set after the commit, because InitialiseNewGame clears every flag that is not story.* and this one has to survive it. Read by dialogue.json's NpcBindings for Bram.

Against the creature standing in front of the player -- its species, its level, the one it has been the whole scene. Routed through EncounterDirector rather than straight at the flow, so it is removed from the world when the player wins or catches it, and runs off if they do not. The prologue's suppression of wild encounters does not apply here; that is what EncounterDirector.TriggerStagedEncounter is for.

The flock breaks. Value false scatters them outward for a beat and then removes them, rather than blinking them out -- a ring that vanishes is a ring that was never there. It has to happen here and not before the battle, because 'field_professor_returns' chains straight off this episode and Linden must not arrive to a bank still ringed by wild Pokemon. The runner's finally clears anything left on every other path out.

Episodes.Note: Where the dex is granted, and where the prologue ends. The grant is the CompletionFlag rather than a SetFlag beat on purpose: the runner sets it the moment the beats finish, so a player whose dialogue timed out or whose walk was snapped still comes out of this holding a Pokedex -- every beat in it degrades rather than throwing, which is what 'finish' means here. A genuinely interrupted run (an exception, a stopped coroutine) now leaves the flag unset instead, and the runner's startup chain-resume replays the episode on the next session; that trade -- one scene repeated versus a save that can never leave the opening act, with the field's own encounters and trainers switched off behind the same flag (see StoryPhase) -- is the right one in both directions. He asks for the dex work rather than being given a reason to hand one over; the thread is his own count from the bank, which is why that scene had to come first. Target length ~40s.

Beats.Note: In from the town side, where 'field_professor_mutters' sent him, and drawn again as he sets off. He arrives to a bag that has been opened and a Pokemon that is not his any more. 8.67 m at 1.4 m/s is 6.2 s of walking and the timeout was 8.0, which is not much room for a path longer than the straight line; widened, because the snap is meant to be a last resort and this is on camera.
5 lines. Alarmed for exactly one of them. The last sends the player to the lab, which is the next act's problem and not this file's.

He goes back up the hill, because he just said he would, and he keeps going until he is out of shot rather than stopping eight metres away and turning round. Leaving him standing on the bank makes 'come to the lab' a lie the player can walk around -- and so does leaving him visible at the top of the path.
The flag that ends the prologue is set immediately after this by the runner's finally. From here the field behaves like a field: grass produces encounters, roamers repopulate, and Kes can be fought.

Episodes.Note:
RETARGETED, not new. It used to fire at the town gate the instant the starter was chosen, chained off 'opening_departure'; the starter is now taken on the lake bank with nobody present and there is no such instant. So it moves to where Kes actually went, and waits for the dex -- which is the same flag that makes him challengeable at all (StoryPhase), so the fight becomes available exactly once and by one route.

It has to stay an episode rather than becoming a plain TrainerController challenge, and the reason is Target='starter_counter': TrainerDefinition has no notion of a party derived from the player's choice and carries a placeholder species id in its place, so a fight started any other way is a fight against nothing. This is why the beat sits on NPC_Rival himself and not on a marker beside him -- TrainerController.StandsDown reads the StoryEncounter on its own GameObject and refuses to notice the player while it is pending, and it can only read one that is there.

Dropped with the move: the two MoveActor beats (both aimed at town markers) and 'riv_after', which was Linden commenting on the battle -- he is at the lab by now and cannot. Target length ~2min including the battle.

Beats.Note: TrainerController plays riv_pre before and riv_lost/riv_won after; all three are on the definition in trainers.json. One creature at level 5, the counter to whatever the player took out of the bag.
